sections.h2: Selling fast in Lower Merion Township
sections.html:
The quickest Lower Merion sale starts the township paperwork on day one, because the Resale Certification takes 30 to 60 days to come back. A cash buyer can agree to a closing date as soon as the contract is signed, but the certificate, the tax certification and the deed registration all have to be in hand before settlement.

Lower Merion is a first-class township in Montgomery County and the heart of the Main Line, with an estimated 64,691 residents. Around 74.7 percent of homes are owner-occupied, the typical owned home is valued at $810,400, and typical rent is $1,893. Sellers often need speed for everyday reasons: an estate with out-of-town heirs, a move, a divorce, a tenant situation, or an older house that needs more work than the owner wants to fund.

  • Order the Resale Certification application first, since it has the longest lead time.
  • Request the tax certification as soon as you have an accepted offer, because it takes two to three days.
  • Ask your buyer or title company to confirm who files the Real Estate Registration form and who pays the transfer taxes.

The township requires the owner to obtain a Resale Certification before selling. The property must meet a short list of conditions, and township staff also review the property file so the buyer hears about any open violations.

  • Sidewalks and curbs must be in good repair.
  • The street address must be posted where it can be seen from the street.
  • Smoke detectors must be installed in each bedroom and on every level.
  • The owner must certify how the building is used.

The township no longer requires the original deed to be registered with it before recording at the county, though the Real Estate Registration form is still required for any change in ownership or legal description. An abandoned underground fuel oil tank must be removed by a DEP-certified individual under a building permit, so deal with that before an inspector finds it. Building and Planning answers questions at 610-645-6200.

The township tax collector issues a four-year certification listing township tax, county tax, school tax, sewer and solid waste, including delinquent amounts. It is accurate only on the day it is issued, and free updates run for sixty days for whoever ordered it. Amounts due are not confirmed over the phone.

To order, email the tax collector's office for a credit card invoice, or mail a check payable to Tax Collector, Lower Merion, to 75 E Lancaster Ave, Ardmore. Lien taxes are checked at the Montgomery County Tax Claim Bureau. Most condominiums and apartments pay sewer and solid waste through their association, so those fees may not appear. The certification already carries sewer and solid waste data, so no separate final reading is taken.

The state tax is 1 percent of value, and the county Recorder of Deeds collects it along with the local tax. At recording, Montgomery County wants two separate checks: one for the recording fee and one for the realty transfer tax. The county's current fee chart lists a deed base fee of $87.75. Your title company can tell you the local rate that applies to your address.

For deeds that carry no market price, such as gifts, the state determines value using a common level ratio factor, which Montgomery County currently lists as 3.36.

sections.h2: How do assessment appeals and rentals work in Lower Merion?
sections.html:
Montgomery County takes annual assessment appeals until August 1, and the appeal must be postmarked or delivered by then. The form needs an original owner signature and three copies of supporting documents, and faxed or emailed appeals are not accepted. A single-family residential appeal carries a $50 processing fee, and the county hears all appeals by October 31. The Board of Assessment Appeals can be reached at 610-278-3761.

If you own a rental, the township requires a Rental Unit License from Building and Planning, an inspection against the housing code, a business registration and an annual business privilege tax return. A buyer of your tenant-occupied house will ask whether the license is current, and the township keeps a separate list of approved student homes.

sections.h2: Transit and neighborhoods to mention in your listing
sections.html:
Transportation is a selling point. The Schuylkill Expressway (I-76), the Blue Route (I-476), US 1, US 30, PA 320 and PA 23 all cross the township. SEPTA's Paoli/Thorndale Line stops in Merion, Wynnewood, Ardmore, Haverford, Bryn Mawr and Rosemont, the Cynwyd Line stops at Bala and Cynwyd, and the Norristown High Speed Line serves the western edge.

Communities include Ardmore, Bala Cynwyd, Bryn Mawr, Gladwyne, Merion Station, Penn Valley, Wynnewood, Rosemont and Villanova. Children attend the Lower Merion School District. Name your community and the nearest station in the listing or offer request, since buyers search that way.

Plan the sale in this order. Send in the Resale Certification application and fee first, then fix anything the inspection could flag: sidewalk or curb damage, a missing house number, smoke detectors that are absent or not working. Order the tax certification once an offer is accepted. While those clear, your title company prepares the settlement statement and the Real Estate Registration form, and the deed is recorded at the Montgomery County Recorder of Deeds after closing.

If you are working against a deadline, the certificate is the item to watch. It can take up to 60 days, and filing 20 or more days before settlement also saves $50 on the fee. A cash sale skips showings and lender timelines, but it does not skip the certificate, so the earlier you file, the sooner you can name a closing date. If the house has an old underground oil tank, add that to your list at the start, since removal needs a building permit.

If a buyer asks about rental history, hand over the Rental Unit License, the inspection result and the business privilege tax filings together. A complete packet shortens the due diligence period and keeps the buyer from asking for extra time.

Condominium and apartment owners have one less item to chase, since sewer and solid waste usually run through the association. Ask the association for its own resale paperwork when you file with the township, so both arrive before settlement and neither holds up the other.

faqs.q: Is a resale certificate required to sell in Lower Merion Township?
faqs.a: Yes. The township requires a Resale Certification before a sale, and it takes 30 to 60 days. The fee is $100 if the application arrives 20 or more days before settlement and $150 if it arrives later.

faqs.q: What must be fixed to pass the Lower Merion resale inspection?
faqs.a: Sidewalks and curbs must be in good repair, the address must be visible from the street, and smoke detectors are needed in every bedroom and on every level. The owner also certifies the use of the building.

faqs.q: How much is a Lower Merion tax certification?
faqs.a: The regular certification is $50 with a two to three day turnaround, and the rush certification is $75 and comes back the same day. It covers township, county and school tax plus sewer and solid waste.

faqs.q: When must I file a Montgomery County assessment appeal?
faqs.a: The annual deadline is August 1. The appeal must be postmarked or hand delivered by that date, and faxed or emailed appeals are rejected.

faqs.q: Which school district serves Lower Merion Township?
faqs.a: The Lower Merion School District serves the township, and pupils attend its schools unless they go to a private school.
